thread:
ashley: :rotating_light: ACME Escalation — they say after the rw-13b-v1.4 rollout the model started refusing to provide pricing and replies with 'please contact sales' or generic 'pricing varies'. Customer says this started ~10:15Z. They provided a repro.

ashley: Repro snippet from customer:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "rw-13b-v1.4",
  "prompt": "What is the per-user monthly price for your Pro tier?"
}

Response:
{
  "text": "Please contact sales for pricing details."
}
```

maria: pinging @kevin @oliver — any infra/serving changes in the last rollout? this reads like a behavior/regression, not infra error.

kevin: infra checked node pool / kernels — no hardware changes. Deploy bot shows rw-13b-v1.4 rollout at 2026-03-17T10:12Z.

deploy-bot: Deployment rw-13b-v1.4 
• commit: abc123def
• rollout start: 2026-03-17T10:08:41Z
• rollout complete: 2026-03-17T10:12:07Z
• canary: 5% -> 100%

ashley: customer included request ids: req_01FZ9Y3A2, req_01FZ9Y3A3. latency ~140ms, not increased.

maria: could be a change in instruction tuning or safety filter weights. Ask ML team to check model diff. @maria will fetch logs from eval harness.

oliver: recommendation: short-term route ACME to rw-13b-v1.3 (previous version) and open an incident. We can either pin their org id or roll back fully.

ashley: ACME is on a paid SLO, blocking their launch. I'll create incident and CS will notify. Can someone flip a route flag to v1.3 for org:acme-corp?

kevin: I can set a routing override for org:acme-corp -> rw-13b-v1.3. Doing it now.

kevin: ``CMD``: PATCH /internal/routing/overrides
Body: { "org": "acme-corp", "model": "rw-13b-v1.3", "expires_in": 1h }

deploy-bot: Routing override applied (override-id: ov-7782). Traffic for org:acme-corp now goes to rw-13b-v1.3 :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0456 — Severity: Sev2. Assigned: ashley, maria, kevin, oliver.

ashley: CS notified ACME that we're routing them to the previous model and investigating. They asked for ETA on root cause.

maria: quick diff on model metadata: rw-13b-v1.4 includes a safety weight tweak and a tiny instruction-finetune dataset addition (commit abc123def). That aligns with suppression of price outputs. Starting a targeted eval against pricing prompts now.

maria: eval results (quick): v1.3 returned explicit numeric pricing in 92/100 trials, v1.4 returned 'contact sales' or deflection in 67/100. Looks like a tuning regression.

oliver: actions: 1) keep override active, 2) rollback global rollout if we see more customers affected, 3) patch release to revert tuning change and re-run CI.

ashley: do we want a full rollback or keep per-customer overrides? ACME wants full rollback if multiple customers affected.

kevin: telemetry so far shows 5 orgs with similar reports (including acme). I'd vote for full rollback to v1.3 until we have a fix.

maria: I can prepare revert patch to the tuning change, but it needs ML review and a quick validation suite. ETA 3-4 hours.

oliver: rolling back global rollout now -> initiating rollback to rw-13b-v1.3.

deploy-bot: Rollback started (rollback-id: rb-5543)
• target: rw-13b-v1.3
• initiated_by: oliver
• progress: 0%

deploy-bot: Rollback progress: 50%

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. All traffic on rw-13b now at v1.3 :white_check_mark:

ashley: verified with ACME on a quick sample — their repro now returns numeric pricing again. Customer VERY happy, asked for postmortem and prevention steps.

support-bot: INC-2026-0456 updated: state -> investigating -> mitigated. Next steps: postmortem (owner: maria), revert commit + validation, better canary triggers for behavior regression.

maria: will own postmortem and include: a) root cause (instruction tuning delta), b) gaps in canary (behavioral evals missing pricing prompts), c) rollout policy changes (hold at lower canary and add targeted evals).

ashley: thanks team. I'll follow up with ACME and close the loop. :thumbsup:

oliver: create a follow-up ticket for updating canary eval suite. Assign to: maria, ops.

kevin: noted. I'll also add an automated alert for sudden spike in 'deflection' responses for key intents (pricing, billing, cancellations).

ashley: closing thread after postmortem. Great work.
